title: Gmail Dictation: How to Dictate Emails in Gmail (2026)
summary: Gmail has no mic on desktop. Here is how to dictate emails on Mac, Windows, Chromebook, Android, and iPhone.
body_markdown:
Most of what we type in a day is email, and most email is short, conversational, and easier to say than to write. So it is a surprise to many people that Gmail has no dictation button. Open the compose window in Chrome and look as long as you like: there is no microphone. Gmail dictation still works, though. It just comes from your computer or your phone rather than from Gmail. This guide shows how to dictate in Gmail on every device, step by step, with the shortcuts and spoken commands that make it fast.


**The short answer:** Gmail on the web has no built-in voice typing, so use your device's dictation instead. Click into the email body, then press the Microphone key (or Fn twice) on a Mac, Windows key + H on Windows, or Search + D on a Chromebook, and speak. In the Gmail app on Android or iPhone, tap the microphone on your keyboard.


The steps below follow Apple's[Mac User Guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/use-dictation-mh40584/mac) , Microsoft's[voice typing guide](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/use-voice-typing-to-talk-instead-of-type-on-your-pc-fec94565-c4bd-329d-e59a-af033fa5689f) , and Google's[Chromebook](https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/12001244) and[Gmail](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/17085010) help pages, as they read at the time of writing.


## Does Gmail have voice typing?


Not in the way people expect. Google's voice typing tool lives in[Google Docs](https://aquavoice.com/blog/google-docs-voice-typing) and Slides; the Gmail compose window has no microphone on the web. On a phone it looks like Gmail is listening, but the microphone you tap belongs to your keyboard (Gboard on Android, Apple's keyboard on iPhone), not to Gmail.


Two Gmail features sound like dictation and are not:


- **Gmail Live** is a voice assistant in the Gmail app on Android and iPhone. Per Google's help page, you talk to it to get answers from your inbox (its example is asking for a flight's gate number). It does not write emails for you. It is in beta, English only, and needs an eligible Google AI or Workspace plan.
- **Help me write** drafts an email from a short prompt. Google's desktop instructions have you type that prompt into a bar at the bottom of the compose window. You can dictate the prompt with the methods below, but the email it produces is Gemini's wording, not yours.


If what you want is your own words in the email body, use your device's dictation.


## How to dictate in Gmail on a Mac


macOS dictation types into any text field, including Gmail in Chrome, Safari, or any other browser.


1. **Turn it on once.** Choose Apple menu, then **System Settings** , click **Keyboard** , and switch on **Dictation** (click **Enable** if asked).
2. **Open Gmail** and click **Compose** , or open a thread and click **Reply** .
3. **Click into the message body** so the cursor sits where the words should go.
4. **Start dictating.** Press the **Microphone** key in the function row (F5 on recent keyboards), use the shortcut chosen under Keyboard, then Dictation, then Shortcut (a common preset is pressing **Fn** twice), or choose **Edit** , then **Start Dictation** .
5. **Speak** at a normal pace. Say "comma," "period," or "new paragraph" where you want them.
6. **Stop** by pressing Escape, the Microphone key, or your shortcut again. Dictation also stops on its own after 30 seconds of silence.


Press and release the Microphone key. Holding it opens Siri instead, which is the most common reason Mac dictation seems broken. Our full guide to[dictation on a Mac](https://aquavoice.com/blog/how-to-use-dictation-on-mac) covers commands, offline use, and Voice Control.


## How to dictate in Gmail on Windows


Windows 11 and Windows 10 include voice typing that works in any browser.


1. Open Gmail and click **Compose** or **Reply** .
2. Click into the message body.
3. Press the **Windows logo key + H** . The voice typing bar appears.
4. Speak. Your words appear at the cursor.
5. Say **"stop listening"** or press Win + H again when you are done.


Click the gear on the voice typing bar and turn on **Automatic punctuation** , which places commas and periods from the way you speak. Without it, say the marks by name: "period," "comma," "question mark," "new line," "new paragraph." Two commands are handy in email: "scratch that" deletes what you just said, and "press Enter" adds a line break. Voice typing needs an internet connection. More in our guide to[voice to text on Windows 11](https://aquavoice.com/blog/voice-to-text-windows) .


## How to dictate in Gmail on a Chromebook


ChromeOS has dictation built into its accessibility settings.


1. Select the time at the bottom right (or press **Alt + Shift + S** ) and open **Settings** .
2. Select **Accessibility** . Under **Keyboard and text input** , turn on **Dictation** .
3. In Gmail, click into the message body.
4. Select the **Speak** button, or press **Search + D** (or **Launcher + D** ), and talk.
5. Say "cancel" to stop.


Google notes that dictation will not work if the language you speak does not match the device language. Chromebook dictation also has editing commands: "delete the previous word," "replace \[phrase\] with \[phrase\]," "new line," "undo," and "select all."


## How to dictate in the Gmail app on Android


1. Open the Gmail app and tap **Compose** , or open an email and tap **Reply** .
2. Tap the body of the message.
3. Tap the **microphone** at the top of the keyboard and speak.


If there is no microphone, open the keyboard settings (the gear in Gboard's top bar), tap **Voice typing** , and turn it on. If it does nothing, give Gboard microphone permission under **Settings** , **Apps** , **Gboard** , **Permissions** , **Microphone** . Our guides to[talk to text on Android](https://aquavoice.com/blog/talk-to-text-android) and[voice to text on a Samsung phone](https://aquavoice.com/blog/voice-to-text-samsung) cover the rest, including spoken punctuation and Pixel's advanced voice typing.


## How to dictate in the Gmail app on iPhone


1. Turn on dictation once: **Settings** , then **General** , then **Keyboard** , then **Enable Dictation** .
2. In the Gmail app, tap **Compose** (or **Reply** ) and tap the message body.
3. Tap the **microphone** on the keyboard and speak.
4. Tap the microphone again, or say "Stop dictation," when you are done.


Say "period," "comma," and "new paragraph" for punctuation and breaks. If the microphone key is missing, check that Enable Dictation is on and that you are on Apple's keyboard, not a third-party one. Full details are in our guide to[voice to text on iPhone](https://aquavoice.com/blog/voice-to-text-iphone) .


## The Google Docs workaround


If your computer's dictation is not an option, Google Docs has its own voice typing in Chrome: open a document, choose **Tools** , then **Voice typing** , click the microphone, and speak. Then copy the text into Gmail. It works, but it is a detour for every email. Our[Google Docs voice typing guide](https://aquavoice.com/blog/google-docs-voice-typing) has the commands.


## Tips for dictating emails that do not need fixing


- **Think in sentences before you start.** Built-in dictation transcribes every word, including "um" and restarts. A pause to plan the sentence saves more time than any command.
- **Dictate the body, type the address.** Email addresses and unusual names are where every dictation tool stumbles. Type the To line and dictate everything else.
- **Say the line breaks.** "New paragraph" after the greeting and before the sign-off gives you a properly spaced email without touching the keyboard.
- **Read it before you hit Send.** Homophones ("their," "there") and misheard names are the usual errors, and they are easy to miss in a quick reply.
- **Use a headset in noisy places.** Background noise is the biggest cause of bad transcripts on every platform.


## Gmail dictation not working? Quick fixes


- **Nothing happens when you press the shortcut.** Check that dictation is switched on in your system settings, and that the cursor is in the message body. Dictation types only into the field that has focus.
- **It cannot hear you.** Check that your microphone is not muted and that the right input device is selected in your sound settings. On a Mac, also check whether Voice Control is on, since standard Dictation is unavailable while it runs.
- **Words come out in the wrong language.** Mac and iPhone follow the dictation language or keyboard you have selected; Windows follows your active keyboard language; Chromebooks need the spoken language to match the device language.
- **It works on Wi-Fi but not on the train.** Windows voice typing needs an internet connection, and so does dictation on many phones and Macs. See our[Mac dictation fixes](https://aquavoice.com/blog/mac-dictation-not-working) for more.


## Where built-in dictation falls short in Gmail


The tools above are free and good enough for a quick reply. Where they run out:


- **Every device works differently.** A different shortcut, different commands, and different quirks on your Mac, your work PC, and your phone.
- **Names and jargon.** Built-in dictation has no dictionary you can fill with clients, colleagues, and product names, so the same words come out wrong every time.
- **Raw transcripts.** It types what you said, fillers and all, so a rambling first take becomes a rambling email.
- **Editing means the keyboard.** Fixing a sentence after it lands usually means selecting and retyping.

## FAQ


### Does Gmail have a dictation button?


No, not on the web. The Gmail compose window has no microphone. On a computer, use your system's dictation (the Microphone key or Fn twice on a Mac, Windows key + H on Windows, Search + D on a Chromebook). In the Gmail app on a phone, tap the microphone on your keyboard.


### How do I dictate an email in Gmail on my phone?


Open the Gmail app, tap Compose or Reply, tap the message body, and tap the microphone on your keyboard. On iPhone, turn on Enable Dictation under Settings, General, Keyboard first. On Android, turn on Voice typing in Gboard's settings if the microphone is missing.


### Can Gmail Live write emails for me?


Not according to Google's help page. Gmail Live is a beta voice assistant in the Gmail app on Android and iPhone that answers questions using your emails, in English, for eligible Google AI and Workspace plans. To put your own words in an email, use dictation.


### Is there a Chrome extension for Gmail dictation?


Several third-party extensions add a microphone to Gmail, but you do not need one: the dictation built into macOS, Windows, and ChromeOS already types into Gmail. A system-wide app such as Aqua also works in Gmail and everywhere else, without an extension.
